# YT Music Scrobbler: Full Product Context

Canonical URL: https://ytscrobbler.kuberbassi.com/
Source: https://github.com/kuberbassi/ytmusic-scrobbler
License: MIT
Creator: Kuber Bassi
Last reviewed: 2026-08-25

## Summary

YT Music Scrobbler is a free, open-source web application that synchronizes newly observed items from YouTube Music history to a user's own Last.fm profile. It is designed for listening that happens across phones, desktop browsers, smart TVs, and Nest devices because it reads the central YouTube Music history rather than depending on an open player tab.

## User workflow

1. Sign in to the application with Google.
2. Create a personal Last.fm API application.
3. Save the Last.fm API key and shared secret, then approve Last.fm authorization.
4. Paste authenticated YouTube Music browser request headers using the in-app setup guide.
5. Enable automatic scrobbling.
6. cron-job.org invokes the protected backend approximately every five minutes, including while the user's browser is closed.

The Last.fm callback URL for API application setup is:
https://ytscrobbler.kuberbassi.com/api/lastfm-callback

The application homepage value is:
https://ytscrobbler.kuberbassi.com/

## Core capabilities

- Cross-device history synchronization
- Five-minute scheduled backend processing
- Manual history refresh and individual/manual scrobbling
- Persistent duplicate protection across serverless instances
- Filtering intended to retain music performances while excluding common non-music content
- Encrypted transport and server-only credential handling
- Google-authenticated, per-user data isolation
- Atomic processing claims to prevent concurrent processing of the same user
- Runtime budgets and retry backoff to control Vercel CPU consumption
- Connection health and actionable expired-session warnings
- Guided Last.fm and YouTube Music setup

## Accuracy and product limitations

YouTube Music history is a snapshot. It does not provide this application with exact playback duration, a reliable event timestamp for every item, or a durable unique identifier for every replay. Therefore:

- The backend can detect newly observed history items.
- It can reliably avoid resubmitting known items.
- It cannot always distinguish a legitimate replay of a known song from the same unchanged history entry.
- Exact replay-aware scrobbling would require a browser extension, desktop application, or mobile companion that observes playback directly.

The application must not be described as perfectly real-time. It is scheduled background synchronization with an approximately five-minute cadence for eligible users.

## Architecture

- Frontend: server-rendered HTML, vanilla JavaScript, and CSS
- Backend: Python and Flask-compatible Vercel Function
- Music integrations: ytmusicapi and pylast/Last.fm Web Services
- Database: Supabase Postgres accessed by a server-only service-role key
- Authentication: Google OAuth for application identity and Last.fm authorization for scrobbling
- Scheduler: cron-job.org with an Authorization Bearer secret
- Hosting: Vercel Fluid Compute

The browser does not poll the backend every few seconds. Status refreshes are event-driven. Routine status reads avoid expensive third-party probes; explicit validation performs a signed Last.fm request and a YouTube Music history check.

## Security and privacy

- Last.fm shared secrets and session keys are stored server-side.
- YouTube Music browser headers are stored server-side.
- Configuration responses expose only boolean configured states, never credential values.
- The cron endpoint requires CRON_SECRET as an Authorization Bearer token.
- Supabase users and scrobbles tables have Row Level Security enabled and grant no read access to anon or authenticated browser roles.
- The service-role key must exist only in the server environment.
- Rate limits protect authentication and scrobble endpoints.

Users should revoke or replace their credentials if they believe the values were exposed. See https://ytscrobbler.kuberbassi.com/privacy and https://ytscrobbler.kuberbassi.com/.well-known/security.txt.

## Data semantics

The database stores users, encrypted or protected integration credentials, settings, synchronization health, processing claims, and bounded track identity aliases used for duplicate protection. A baseline is captured when new YouTube Music headers are connected so old history is not submitted as new listening.

Successful synchronization updates last_sync_success_at. Failures record a bounded error and increase retry backoff. Stale claims expire so a failed function invocation cannot permanently lock a user.
